en: a. very large in amount or degree; extremely good or impressive; (informal) very great
ex: The team made a tremendous effort to win the game.
球隊為贏得比賽付出了極大的努力。

en: n. a small thin branch of a tree or bush; a very thin piece of wood; v. (British, informal) to suddenly understand something
ex: The bird built a nest out of twigs.
那隻鳥用細樹枝築了一個巢。

en: n. a strong wish or need to do something; a strong push to do something; vt. to strongly encourage someone to do something; to push someone or something in a particular direction; vi. to ask for something strongly
ex: She felt an urge to laugh during the serious meeting.
在嚴肅的會議中，她有一股想笑的衝動。

en: n. a room in a hotel that is available for guests; a job that is not yet filled; an empty space; a lack of ideas or interest
ex: The hotel has no vacancies this weekend.
這家飯店這個週末沒有空房。

en: n. a large boat or ship; a container for holding liquids; a tube in the body that carries blood or other liquids; a large ship used for carrying goods or passengers
ex: A large vessel was anchored in the harbor.
一艘大船停泊在港口。

en: vt. to break a law, rule or agreement; to treat something holy with no respect; to disturb someone's privacy; to cause harm to something
ex: Drivers who violate traffic laws will be fined.
違反交通規則的駕駛人將被罰款。

en: n. a very small living thing that causes disease in people, animals and plants; an illness caused by a virus; a program that damages a computer system
ex: The flu virus spreads quickly in winter.
流感病毒在冬天傳播得很快。

en: a. done because you want to and not because you are forced to; done without payment; (of a muscle or action) controlled by the will; n. a piece of music played on an organ
ex: Joining the club is entirely voluntary.
加入社團完全是自願的。

en: n. the ability to say or write things that are clever and funny; a person who makes clever, funny remarks; intelligence or good sense; (plural) the ability to think quickly
ex: He is known for his quick wit.
他以機智敏捷聞名。
ph: scare someone out of their wits

en: n. a period of physical exercise to improve your health and fitness; a test or a trial of something; a set of exercises
ex: I do a thirty-minute workout every morning.
我每天早上做三十分鐘的運動。

en: n. a ship that has been destroyed at sea; the remains of something that has been badly damaged; a person or thing in very bad condition; vt. to completely destroy something; vi. (of a ship) to be destroyed at sea
ex: The wreck of the ship was found on the seabed.
那艘船的殘骸在海床上被發現。

en: a. looking, feeling or behaving young; characteristic of young people; full of energy and enthusiasm
ex: She has a youthful appearance despite her age.
她雖然年紀不小，看起來仍很年輕。

en: vt. to make something known that was previously secret; to allow something to be seen; to give information about something
ex: The company refused to disclose the details of the deal.
公司拒絕透露交易的細節。

en: n. a mark or spot that is difficult to remove; a bad point in someone's reputation; a liquid used to color wood; vt. to make something dirty; to change the color of something; vi. to become dirty or discolored
ex: There is a coffee stain on my shirt.
我的襯衫上有咖啡漬。

en: n. a medical procedure to end a pregnancy before the baby can survive; (formal) the early end of a pregnancy; the failure of a plan or process; an event that ends early or fails
ex: The abortion of the mission was announced by the government.
政府宣布了任務的中止。

en: a. very large, heavy and solid; extremely large in size, amount or degree; (of a person or thing) strong and impressive
ex: A massive rock blocked the road after the landslide.
土石流後，一塊巨石擋住了道路。

en: n. something that you say or do to show respect for someone; a payment made by a weak ruler to a stronger one; a sign that something is good; (old) a gift
ex: Many people paid tribute to the late singer.
許多人向已故歌手致敬。

en: vt. to find out something that was hidden or secret; to remove a cover from something; vi. to take off your hat as a sign of respect
ex: Journalists uncovered a major scandal.
記者揭露了一起重大醜聞。

en: n. a group of ships under one commander; a group of vehicles such as taxis or buses owned by one company; a. very fast; (of a stream) shallow; adv. in a shallow way
ex: The fleet sailed out of the harbor at dawn.
艦隊黎明時駛出港口。

en: n. a person who sells meat; a person whose job is to kill animals for food; a cruel person who kills many people; vt. to kill animals for food; to kill people cruelly
ex: I bought a kilo of beef at the butcher's.
我在肉店買了一公斤牛肉。

en: a. not important or serious; of little value; (of a person) not thinking about important things; common and ordinary
ex: Don't worry about such a trivial matter.
別為這種瑣事擔心。

en: n. a large pile of things arranged one on top of another; a large amount of something; a chimney; a place where books are stored in a library; vt. to put things in a pile; to arrange something so that someone has an unfair advantage; vi. to be in a pile
ex: She put a stack of books on the table.
她在桌上放了一疊書。

en: n. a person who starts a business and takes financial risks in the hope of making a profit
ex: The young entrepreneur started her own software company.
那位年輕創業家創辦了自己的軟體公司。

en: n. the act of moving something or someone from one place to another; the act of getting rid of something; the act of taking someone out of a job; the act of taking something out of the body
ex: The removal of the old furniture took two hours.
搬走舊傢俱花了兩小時。

en: n. a complete path that an electric current can flow around; a circular route or track; a series of places or events that happen in order; a group of sports events that take place in a series
ex: The electrician checked the circuit for faults.
電工檢查電路有沒有故障。

en: n. the art and science of designing and making buildings; the style in which a building is designed; the structure of a building; the structure of a computer system
ex: She is studying architecture at university.
她在大學主修建築。

en: n. a light shoe with straps that is worn in warm weather; a shoe with a thin sole and straps; a fragrant wood from a tropical tree
ex: She wore sandals to the beach.
她穿涼鞋去海灘。

en: n. a person who has been officially suggested for a prize, job or election; a person who is chosen for a particular position
ex: She is a nominee for the Best Actress award.
她入圍最佳女主角獎。

en: n. the people who work for a company or organization; the department of an organization that deals with employees; (military) people serving in the armed forces
ex: All personnel must wear safety helmets on site.
所有人員在工地都必須戴安全帽。

en: n. a law or set of laws made by a government; the process of making laws; the act of making something legal
ex: The government introduced new legislation to protect the environment.
政府推出了新法規來保護環境。

en: vt. to expect something to happen and be ready for it; to do something before someone else; to look forward to something; to use something before the proper time
ex: We anticipate a large crowd at the concert.
我們預計演唱會會有大批人潮。

en: vt. to watch over a job or person to make sure that everything is done correctly; to look down on something from above; to notice something by chance; to be responsible for a group
ex: He oversees the production of the entire factory.
他監督整間工廠的生產。

en: n. a stage in a process of change or development; one part of a series of events; one of the ways in which the moon appears to change shape; vt. to introduce something in stages
ex: The project is in the final phase of development.
這個專案處於開發的最後階段。

en: n. a book, film or play with an exciting story, usually about crime; something very exciting; a story that is intended to make people feel afraid
ex: I stayed up all night reading a psychological thriller.
我整晚熬夜讀一本心理驚悚小說。

en: a. not supporting either side in an argument or war; having no strong color; (of an electrical wire) not carrying a charge; n. a country that does not support either side in a war; the position in a car in which the gears are not connected
ex: Switzerland remained neutral during the war.
瑞士在戰爭期間保持中立。

en: vt. to control the direction in which a vehicle, boat or aircraft moves; to guide someone in a particular direction; to control the way something develops; vi. to drive or control a vehicle; n. a young male cow; a piece of advice
ex: She steered the boat safely into the harbor.
她安全地把船駛進了港口。

en: n. permission given by a company to someone to sell its products or services in a particular place; the right to vote; a special right or privilege; vt. to give permission to someone to sell a company's products
ex: He bought a franchise of a famous fast-food chain.
他買下一家知名速食連鎖店的加盟權。

en: n. an area of land where fruit trees are grown; a place where fruit trees are planted in rows
ex: We picked apples in the orchard.
我們在果園裡摘蘋果。

en: n. the act of getting involved in a situation when you are not wanted; something that stops a radio signal from being received clearly; the act of preventing something from happening or developing; (in sport) illegal contact with an opponent
ex: There was a lot of interference on the phone line.
電話線路有很多雜音。

en: n. a formal event with special traditional actions; the formal ways of behaving at a particular event; formal politeness
ex: The graduation ceremony was held in the school auditorium.
畢業典禮在學校禮堂舉行。
